answer: Each epoch the server issues a fresh seed, a pearl of randomness no node can know early, so cached answers from old rounds are worthless. The node must hash its own local state with that seed and return a commitment the server recomputes before counting. Copying a peer fails because the commitment is tied to the node's key, and a willow of stale replies will not match the new seed. Forging takes real compute and locked stake per attempt, and any guess that misses gets slashed, so a single ember of cheating costs more than the reward it could earn.
